0.zh: 第一部分　客观逻辑

en: The complete transformation which the philosophical mode of thinking has undergone among us for the last twenty-five years or so, and the higher standpoint which the self-consciousness of Spirit has attained over itself in this period, have so far had little influence upon the shape of logic.
zh: 近二十五年来，哲学的思维方式在我们中间所经历的彻底改变，以及精神在这一时期通过自我意识而在自身之上达到的更高立场，迄今对逻辑学的形态还很少产生影响。

en: What was called metaphysics before this period has, so to speak, been eradicated root and branch and has vanished from the series of the sciences.
Where are the voices of the former ontology, of rational psychology, of cosmology, or even of the former natural theology still to be heard, or where may they still be heard?
Investigations, for example, into the immateriality of the soul, into the mediating causes and the final causes, where should they still find an interest?
The other proofs of the existence of God are likewise adduced only historically, or for the sake of edification and elevation of the mind.
It is a fact that the interest in the former metaphysics has been lost, partly in its content, partly in its form, and partly in both at once.

As remarkable as it is when a people has become unable to use the science of its state law, when its convictions, its ethical customs and virtues have become useless to it, so remarkable is it at least when a people loses its metaphysics, when the Spirit, occupied with its own pure essence, no longer has any actual existence in it.
zh: 在这个时期之前被称作形而上学的东西，可以说已被连根拔除，从科学的行列中消失了。
从前的本体论、理性心理学、宇宙论，乃至从前的自然神学的声音，还能从哪里发出，又还能从哪里被听到呢？
例如关于灵魂非物质性的研究，关于中介原因与终极原因的研究，它们还能在哪里找到兴趣呢？
其余关于上帝的存在的证明，同样只是出于历史的考虑，或者为了感化与提升心灵而被援引。
这是一个事实：对从前形而上学的兴趣，无论是就其内容、就其形式，还是就两者同时而言，都已失去。
一个民族若对自己的国家法科学、对自己的信念、伦理习俗与德性都已不再适用，那是值得注意的；而一个民族若失去了自己的形而上学，专注于自身纯粹本质的精神在其中不再有任何现实的定在，那至少同样是值得注意的。

en: The exoteric doctrine of the Kantian philosophy — that the understanding must not soar beyond experience, otherwise the faculty of cognition becomes theoretical reason, which for its own part engenders nothing but brain-spun phantasms — has justified, from the scientific side, the renunciation of speculative thinking.

Against this popular doctrine there were the cries of modern pedagogy and the necessity of the times, which direct the gaze to immediate need, maintaining that just as experience is the first thing for cognition, so for skill in public and private life theoretical insight is even harmful, and exercise and practical formation are in general the essential and only thing that promotes.

— Thus, science and the common sense of ordinary men working hand in hand to bring about the downfall of metaphysics, it seemed that the strange spectacle was being brought about of seeing a cultivated people without metaphysics, like a temple otherwise most variously adorned but without the Holy of Holies.

— The theology which in earlier times was the keeper of the speculative mysteries and of the although dependent metaphysics had abandoned this science in favour of feelings, in favour of the practical and popular, and of learned history.

Corresponding to this change is the fact that elsewhere those solitaries who were sacrificed by their people and removed from the world disappeared, to the end that contemplation of the eternal and a life devoted to it alone might exist — not for the sake of any benefit, but for the sake of blessing; a disappearance which, in another connection, can in its essence be regarded as the same appearance as the one just mentioned.

— So that, after the driving out of this darkness, of this colourless occupation of the Spirit turned back upon itself, existence seemed to be transformed into the cheerful world of flowers, among which, as is well known, there is no black one.
zh: 康德哲学的外显学说——即知性不得飞越经验，否则认识能力就变成理论理性，而理论理性本身只能生出头脑编织出来的幻影——从科学这一面为放弃思辨的思维作了辩护。
与这种流行学说相抗衡的，是现代教育学的叫嚷，是那把目光投向直接需要的时代的必需：它主张，正如对认识来说经验是第一位的，那么对公共生活与私人生活中的灵巧来说，理论洞察甚至是有害的，而练习与实际教养才是根本上唯一有促进作用的。
——这样，科学与常人的常识携手促成形而上学的覆亡，仿佛一场奇特的景观被促成了：看到一个有教养的民族竟没有形而上学——就像一座原本装饰得绚丽多彩的庙宇却缺少了至圣所。
——神学在早期时代本是思辨的奥秘与虽属依附的形而上学的守护者，然而它已经放弃了这门科学，转向了情感，转向了实践与通俗的一面，转向了有学问的历史。
与这一变化相应的是：别处那些被自己民族献祭、被逐出世界的孤独者消失了，其目的是使对永恒者的沉思以及一种只侍奉它的生活得以存在——不是为了任何功利，而是为了福祉；这种消失在另一种关联中，就其本质而言，可以看作与刚才所说的同一现象。
——于是，在这些黑暗被驱逐之后，在精神转身向内的无色忙碌被驱逐之后，定在仿佛已被转化为花朵的明朗世界，而在这些花里，众所周知是没有黑色的。

en: The fate of logic has not been much better than that of metaphysics.

The prejudice that one learns through logic to think what otherwise was regarded as useful for it, and thereby for its purpose — as though one first had to learn to digest and to move through the study of anatomy and physiology — has long since been lost, and the spirit of the practical had probably assigned logic no better fate than that of its sister.
Nevertheless, probably for the sake of some formal advantage, a rank among the sciences was still left to it; indeed it was even retained as a subject of public instruction.

This better lot, however, concerns only the external fate; for its shape and content have remained the same as what was handed down through a long tradition, but had in this transmission become more and more diluted and emaciated; the new Spirit which has arisen, not less upon the science than upon actuality, has not yet been felt in it.

But it is altogether in vain, when the substantial form of the Spirit has changed itself, to want to preserve the forms of earlier formation; they are withered leaves, which are shaken off by the new buds which are already forming at their roots.
zh: 逻辑学的命运并不比形而上学的命运好到哪里去。
认为要通过逻辑学才能学会思考那些原本被看作对逻辑学有用、并因而对它的目的有用的东西——就仿佛人必须先通过研究解剖学与生理学，才能学会消化与运动——这种成见早已消失；而务实的精神大概也不会给逻辑学安排比它姊妹更好的命运。
尽管如此，大概是为了某种形式上的益处，逻辑学在诸科学之中仍被保留了一个位次；它甚至被作为公共教学的一门科目保留了下来。
不过，这个较好的命运只涉及外在的命运；因为它的形态与内容仍旧是那个通过悠久的传统传承下来的东西，只不过在传承中变得越来越稀薄、越来越干瘪；那个在科学上并不少于在现实性上已经涌现的新精神，尚未在它身上显露出来。
然而，当精神的实体形式已经改变自身之后，还想保留早先形成的那些形式，是一劳永逸地徒劳的；它们是枯萎的叶子，会被那些已经在其根部生成的新芽抖落。

en: With the ignoring of the general change, it is beginning to happen, little by little, even in the matter of science.

Unnoticed, the other representations have even become familiar and proper to the opponents themselves; and if they continue to act brittle towards their source and principles and behave towards them in a self-contradictory way, they have submitted to the consequences and have been unable to ward off their influence; for their negative behaviour, which keeps becoming more insignificant, they know no other way of giving themselves a positive importance and content than by joining in with the new modes of representation.
zh: 随着对这一普遍变化的漠视，即使在科学领域里，也开始渐渐地出现这种情况。
在不知不觉中，就连反对者也已熟悉并习惯了别的表象；当他们仍旧对那些表象的来源与原则显得僵硬、并且自相矛盾地反对它们时，他们已经接受了这些后果，并且无法抵挡它们的影响；由于他们那越来越无足轻重的否定态度，他们除了在新表象方式中插话之外，再没有别的办法为自己赢得积极的重要性与内容。

en: On the other hand, it seems that the time of fermentation, with which a new creation begins, is past.

In its first appearance such a time is accustomed to behave with fanatical hostility towards the widespread systematization of the earlier principle, partly also to be afraid of losing itself in the extension of the particular, partly however to shun the labour required for scientific formation and, in need of one, to have recourse at once to an empty formalism.
The demand for the working up and formation of the material now becomes ever more urgent.
It is a period in the formation of an age, as in the formation of the individual, in which it is above all about the acquisition and the assertion of the principle in its undeveloped intensity.
But the higher requirement is directed toward its becoming science.
zh: 从另一方面看，那种孕育着新创造的发酵时期似乎已经过去了。
这种时期在最初出现时，惯于以狂热的敌意对待早已铺开的对先前原则的体系化；有时它也害怕在特殊性的扩展中迷失自己，有时又躲避科学陶冶所必需的工作，而在需要它的时候，一开始就抓住一种空洞的形式主义。
于是，对材料的加工与陶冶的要求变得越来越迫切。
这这是一个时代的形成期，正如个体的形成期一样，在这里首要的在于获取原则，并在它尚未展开的强度上加以主张。
但更高的要求指向的是：它要成为科学。

en: Whatever may already have been done for the subject matter and the form of the science in other respects, the logical science, which constitutes the proper metaphysics or pure speculative philosophy, has so far been very much neglected.
What I understand more precisely by this science and its standpoint, I have indicated provisionally in the Introduction.

The necessity of beginning afresh with this science once more, the nature of the subject itself, and the want of preparatory works which might have been used for the transformation undertaken, may be taken into account by cheap judgements, even though a many years' labour could not give this attempt a greater perfection.
— The essential point of view is that the question is at all about a new conception of scientific treatment.

Philosophy, in so far as it is to be science, cannot, as I have remarked elsewhere1, borrow its method for this from a subordinate science such as mathematics, any more than it can content itself with categorical assertions of inner intuition or use ratiocination on grounds of external reflection.
Rather, it can only be the nature of the content which moves in scientific cognition; for it is this own reflection of the content which at the same time first posits and produces its determination.
zh: 无论就这门科学的对象与形式而言此前在其他方面已经做了些什么，逻辑科学——它构成真正的形而上学或纯粹思辨哲学——迄今都还大大地被忽略了。
我对这门科学及其立场更确切的理解，已在《导言》中作了初步的说明。
不得不再次从头开始处理这门科学的必然性、对象本身的性质，以及本可用于这次改造的前期工作之缺乏，这些都可以由轻率的评判者来权衡，尽管多年的努力也未能使这次尝试达到更高的完善。
——根本的着眼点在于：问题归根结底是关于科学处理的一种新概念。
哲学既然应当是科学，就不能像我在别处指出的那样，为此从一门从属的科学（数学就是这样的科学）借取其方法，同样也不能满足于对内在直观的断言式担保，或出于外在反思的缘故而诉诸推理。
而只能是内容的性质在科学认识中运动；因为正是内容自身的这种反思，才同时首先设定并产生出这一规定。

en: The understanding determines and holds fast the determinations; reason is negative and dialectical, because it dissolves the determinations of the understanding into nothing; it is positive because it produces the universal and comprehends the particular in it.
Just as the understanding is generally taken as something separate from reason, so the dialectical reason is also usually taken as something separate from the positive reason.
But in its truth reason is Spirit, which is higher than both, intelligible reason or rational understanding.

It is the negative, that which constitutes the quality both of dialectical reason and of the understanding; — it negates the simple, and so it posits the determinate difference of the understanding; it dissolves that difference just as much, and so it is dialectical.

But it does not remain in the nothing of this result, but is just as positive in it and has thereby established the first simple, but as a universal which is concrete in itself; under this, no given particular is subsumed, but in that determination and in the dissolution of the same the particular has already determined itself along with it.

This spiritual movement, which in its simplicity gives itself its determinateness and in this determinateness its equality with itself, and which is thereby the immanent development of the concept, is the absolute method of cognition and at the same time the immanent soul of the content itself.
— On this self-constructing path alone, I assert, philosophy is capable of being objective, demonstrated science.
— In this way I have attempted to present consciousness in the Phenomenology of Spirit.

Consciousness is Spirit as concrete knowledge, and indeed knowledge entangled in externality; but the onward movement of this subject rests, like the development of all natural and spiritual life, solely on the nature of the pure essences which constitute the content of logic.

Consciousness, as the appearing Spirit which frees itself on its way from its immediacy and external determinacy, becomes pure knowledge, which makes those pure essences themselves, as they are in and for themselves, its object.
They are the pure thoughts, the Spirit which thinks its essence.
Their self-movement is their spiritual life and is that by which science constitutes itself and of which it is the exposition.
zh: 知性规定并固定这些规定；理性是否定而辩证的，因为它把知性的规定化解为无；理性又是肯定的，因为它产生普遍者，并在其中以概念把握特殊者。
正像人们通常把知性看作与理性相分离的东西一样，人们也惯于把辩证的理性看作与肯定的理性相分离的东西。
但就其真理而言，理性是精神，是高于二者的东西，是可理解的理性或合乎理性的知性。
它是否定者，是构成辩证理性与知性两者的质的东西；——它否定单纯者，于是它设定知性的规定差别；它同样消解这一差别，于是它是辩证的。
但它并不停留于这一结果的空无之中，而是在其中同样是肯定的；这样它就建立起第一个单纯者，但这个单纯者是一个在自身具体的普遍者；在它之下并不是把一个现成的特殊者归摄进去，而是在那种规定与对它的消解之中，特殊者本身已经随之得到规定。
这种精神的运动在其单纯性中赋予自身以规定性，并在这一规定性中赋予自身以同自身的同一；它因此就是概念的内在发展，是认识的绝对方法，同时也是内容自身的内在灵魂。
——我主张，只有在这条自我构造的道路上，哲学才有能力成为客观的、经过论证的科学。
——我曾试图以这样的方式，在《精神现象学》中呈现意识。
意识是精神，作为具体的、因而在外在性中受局限的知识；但这一对象的推进却单单——正如一切自然生活与精神生活的发展一样——建立在构成逻辑学内容的纯粹本质的性质之上。
意识作为显现的精神，在其行程中从自身的直接性与外在的具体性中解放出来，成为纯粹的知识，它把那些纯粹本质本身——如它们自在自为的那样——当作自己的对象。
它们是纯粹的思想，是那个以思维为本质的精神。
它们的自我运动就是它们的精神生命，是科学借以自我构成的东西，也是科学所表述的东西。

en: The relation of the science which I call the Phenomenology of Spirit to logic is hereby indicated.

— As for the external relation, the first part of the system of science2, which contains the Phenomenology, was destined to be followed by a second part, which was to contain logic and the two real sciences of philosophy, the philosophy of nature and the philosophy of Spirit, and would have concluded the system of science.

But the necessary expansion which logic had to obtain for itself has induced me to let it come to the fore especially; it therefore constitutes in an extended plan the first sequel to the Phenomenology of Spirit.
Later I shall let the treatment of the two real sciences of philosophy just named follow.

— This first volume of logic contains, as its first book, the doctrine of Being, the second book, the doctrine of Essence, as the second division of the first volume; the second volume will contain subjective logic or the doctrine of the Concept.
zh: 至此，我称之为《精神现象学》的这门科学与逻辑学的关系已经说明。
——就外在关系而言，这门科学的体系2的第一部分（其中包含《精神现象学》）原定要有一个第二部分跟上，那一部分应当包含逻辑学以及哲学的两门实在的科学——自然哲学与精神哲学——并以此结束整个科学的体系。
但逻辑学为自身所必需的扩展促使我让它特别地显露出来；于是在一个扩充了的计划中，它便构成了对《精神现象学》的第一部续篇。
此后我将继续处理上面提到的哲学的两门实在的科学。
——逻辑学的这第一卷以第一篇包含存在的学说，以第二篇即本质的学说作为第一卷的第二部分；第二卷则将包含主观逻辑，即概念的学说。

en: Nuremberg, 22. March 1812
zh: 纽伦堡，1812 年 3 月 22. 日

en: I have undertaken this new treatment of the science of logic, of which the first volume now appears, fully aware both of the difficulty of the subject in itself and then of its exposition, as well as of the incompleteness which the treatment of it in the first edition carries with it; although after further many years' occupation with this science I had striven to remedy this incompleteness, I still feel I have good reason to claim the indulgence of the reader.
A title of such a claim may indeed in the first place be grounded on the circumstance that for the content one has found in the earlier metaphysics and logic only external material.

However generally and frequently the same has been worked on — the latter continued right up to our own times — so little did such treatment touch the speculative side; rather, on the whole, the same material has been repeated, alternately now diluted to trivial superficiality, now fetched up anew and dragged along with it the old ballast in greater bulk, so that through such, often quite merely mechanical, labours no gain could accrue to the philosophical content.

To present the realm of thought philosophically, i.e. in its own immanent activity or, what is the same, in its necessary development, must therefore have been a new undertaking and had to be begun from the very beginning; that acquired material, those known forms of thought, must, however, be regarded as a most important template, indeed a necessary condition and a premise to be gratefully acknowledged, even if it only gives here and there a thin thread or the lifeless bones of a skeleton, even thrown together disorderly among themselves.
zh: 我着手重新处理逻辑学这门科学——现在呈现出来的是它的第一卷——时，完全意识到两方面的难处：对象本身的困难以及它的表述，还有第一版对它的处理所带有的那种不完善；尽管我在此后多年继续钻研这门科学时，我曾努力想弥补这种不完善，我仍然感到自己有充分理由请求读者的宽容。
而书名所作的这种要求，首先大概可以建立在这样的情形之上：在早先的形而上学与逻辑学中，人们为内容找到的主要只是外在的材料。
同样的材料被如此普遍而频繁地加工着——后者一直延续到我们的时代——却如此少地触及思辨的一面；相反，整体上被重复的始终是同一份材料，时而稀薄到流于琐屑的表面化，时而又把旧有的重负重新更大规模地翻出来并拖带着，以致通过这些往往纯属机械的劳作，哲学内容不可能有任何增长。
因此，要在哲学的意义上——即在思想自身的内在活动中，或在它必然的发展中——把思想的领域表述出来，就必定是一项全新的事业，而且必须从头做起；不过，那些已经获取的材料、那些为人熟知的思维形式，却应当被视为一份极其重要的底本，乃至一个必要条件、一个应当心存感激地予以承认的前提，即使它所能提供的不过是些稀疏的线头或一副骨架的无生命的骨头，甚至是被杂乱无章地堆在一起的。

en: The forms of thought are first of all set forth and deposited in the language of man; in our days it cannot be reminded often enough that that whereby man is distinguished from the animal is thinking.

Into everything which becomes an inner thing for him, a representation at all, whatever he makes his own, language has pressed itself; and whatever he makes into language and expresses in it contains a category, whether wrapped up, mixed in, or worked out; so very natural is the logical to him, or rather: that very thing is his peculiar nature itself.

But if one confronts nature in general, as the physical, with the spiritual, one would have to say that the logical is rather the supernatural, which presses into all the natural behaviour of man, into his feeling, his intuiting, his desiring, his needing, his urging, and thereby makes it at all into something human — even if only formally — into representations and purposes.

It is an advantage of a language when it possesses a wealth of logical expressions, namely proper and separated ones, for the determinations of thought themselves; of the prepositions and articles many already belong to such relations as are based on thinking; the Chinese language is said not to have reached that at all in its development, or only scantily; but these particles appear quite in the service, only a little more detached than the augmentations, the inflectional signs and the like.

Far more important is it that in a language the determinations of thought are set out as nouns and verbs and are thus stamped into an objective form; the German language has in this many advantages over the other modern languages; indeed some of its words have the further peculiarity of having not only different meanings but opposite ones, so that a speculative spirit of the language is not to be unrecognized in it; it can afford the thinking a pleasure to come upon such words and to find the unification of opposites — which result of speculation is yet nonsense for the understanding — already lexically, in a naive fashion, presented as one word with opposite meanings.

Philosophy therefore needs no special terminology at all; a few words are indeed to be taken over from foreign languages, which however have already acquired citizenship in it through use; — an affected purism would be least in place precisely where the matter itself is most at stake.

— The advance of formation in general, and especially of the sciences, even the empirical and sensible ones, in so far as they move in general in the most ordinary categories (e.g. of a whole and its parts, of a thing and its properties and the like), gradually also brings to light higher relations of thought, or at least lifts them up to greater universality and thereby to closer attention.

If, for example, in physics the determination of thought of force has become predominant, then in recent times the category of polarity — which, incidentally, has intruded far too much à tort et à travers into everything, even into light — plays the most significant role, — the determination of a difference in which the different are inseparably united; that in this way one proceeds from the form of abstraction, of identity, through which a determinacy such as force gains a self-sufficiency, and that the form of determination, of difference, which at the same time remains as an inseparable in identity, is lifted out and has become a current representation, is of infinite importance.

The consideration of nature brings with it, through the reality in which its objects hold fast, this compulsion: to fix the categories which can no longer be ignored in it, even if with the greatest inconsistency towards others which are also allowed to hold, and not to permit that, as happens more easily in the spiritual, one passes over to abstractions from the opposition and to generalities.
zh: 思维形式首先是在人的语言中被树立并安放下来的；在我们今天的日子里，再怎么反复提醒也不为过：使人与动物相区别的东西就是思维。
语言已经渗入到他使之成为内在的、成为某种表象的一切东西之中，即他据为己有的一切东西之中；而他使之成为语言并在语言中表达出来的一切，无论是被包裹着的、混杂着的，还是被提炼出来的，都包含着一个范畴；逻辑的东西对他来说是如此自然，或者更确切地说：这个东西本身就是他的独特本性。
但如果把自然整体、作为物理的东西，与精神相对立起来，那就必须说，逻辑的东西毋宁是超自然的东西：它渗入人的一切自然行为，渗入他的感受、直观、欲求、需要与冲动，并由此使它总体上成为属人的东西——哪怕只是形式上的——成为表象与目的。
一门语言若自身为思维规定备有一份逻辑表达的财富——即专属于思维规定、与之分开的表达——那就是这门语言的优势；在介词与冠词之中，已经有许多属于以思维为基础的那些关系；据说汉语在其发展中对这一点根本没有达到，或者只达到微薄的程度；但这些虚词完全是服役性地出现，只比那些增音前缀、屈折标记之类稍稍分离一些而已。

更为重要的是：在一门语言中，思维规定被树立为名词和动词，并因此被打上客观形式的印记；德语在这方面比别的现代语言有许多长处；甚至它有些词还具有一种进一步的特性——不仅有多种意义，而且有相反的意义——以致一种思辨的精神——语言的精神——在那里本身是不可错认的；思维遇到这样的词时会感到愉悦，因为对立者的统一——这一思辨的结果对知性来说还是荒谬的——在这里已经以朴素的词书方式被当作一个具有相反意义的词呈现出来了。
因此哲学根本不需要专门的术语；诚然要从外来语言中采纳一些词，但这些词通过使用已经在那门语言里取得了公民权；——一种矫揉造作的纯粹主义，恰恰在最关系到事情本身的地方最不相宜。
——形成过程本身的推进，特别是科学的推进——即便那些经验的与感性的科学——因为它们总体上是在最普通的范畴中活动的（例如整体与部分、事物及其属性之类），也会逐渐把更高的思维关系带到光天化日之下，或者至少把它们提升到更大的普遍性、因而提升到更密切的注意。

比如说，如果物理学中思维规定「力」取得了支配地位，那么近来人极性这一范畴——它此外已经过分地 à tort et à travers 地侵入了一切，甚至侵入光——就扮演着最重要的角色；——即对这样一个差别的规定，在这一差别中相异者是不可分地联系着的；从抽象的形式、同一性的形式出发（力这一规定性正是通过它获得自身的独立性），并把规定性的形式、即差别的形式——它同时作为不可分者留在同一性之中——提升出来而成为通行的表象，这一过程具有无穷的重要性。
自然考察通过其对象据以持存的实在性，带来了这种强制性：把其中已不能再被漠视的范畴固定下来，即便对另一些同样被容许保留的范畴表现出极大的不一致；并且不容许像在精神领域里较为容易发生的那样，转向对对立面的抽象并走向普遍性。

en: But although the logical objects and their expressions are roughly well known in formation, what is known is for that reason not known, as I have said elsewhere; and it can even arouse impatience that one should still have to occupy oneself with what is already known, — and what is better known than precisely those determinations of thought of which we make use everywhere, which issue from our mouths in every sentence we speak?

This preface is destined to indicate the general moments of the course of cognition starting from this known, and of the relation of scientific thinking to this natural thinking; so much, taken together with what the earlier Introduction contains, will be sufficient to give a general conception of the sense of logical cognition, such a conception as one demands to have in advance of a science — in advance of the science which is the thing itself.
zh: 不过，虽然逻辑的对象及其表达在形成中大致是众所周知的，但如我在别处所说，众所周知的东西正因此并没有被认识；而且甚至会引起不耐烦：人们还得去从事那众所周知的东西；——而还有什么比思维规定更众所周知呢？我们在各处都使用它们，它们在我们所说的每一句话里都从我们口中溜出来。
本序言的任务，正是要指出从这一已知者出发的认识进程的一般环节，指出科学的思维与这种自然的思维之间的关系的一般环节；这些内容，连同早先《导言》所包含的内容一起，将足以给出关于逻辑认识之意味的一种总体表象——那种人们在一门科学之前、即在作为事情本身的那门科学之前所要求的总体表象。

en: First of all, it is to be regarded as an infinite advance that the forms of thought have been freed from the material in which they are immersed in self-conscious intuiting and representing, as in our desiring and willing, or rather also in the representing desiring and willing (and there is no human desiring or willing without representing), that these generalities have been lifted out for themselves and, as Plato first, but then Aristotle above all did, have been made into an object of contemplation for themselves; this gives the beginning of their cognition. "Only after almost everything necessary," says Aristotle, "and what belongs to the convenience and intercourse of life, was already in existence, did men begin to strive after philosophical cognition." "In Egypt," he had remarked before, "the mathematical sciences were developed early, because the priestly caste there was early placed in a position to have leisure."

— Indeed the need to occupy oneself with pure thoughts presupposes a long course which the human spirit must have gone through; it is, one may say, the need of the already satisfied need of necessity, of needlessness to which it must have come, of abstraction from the material of intuition, of imagining and the like, of the concrete interests of desire, of the drives, of the will, in which material the determinations of thought are wrapped up.

In the quiet spaces of the thinking which has come to itself and is only in itself, the interests which move the life of peoples and individuals are silent. "After so many pages," says Aristotle in the same connection, "the nature of man is dependent; but this science, which is not sought for any use, alone is free in and for itself, and it therefore seems not to be a human possession." — Philosophy in general still has to do in its thoughts with concrete objects, God, nature, spirit, but logic concerns itself exclusively with these in themselves in their complete abstraction.

This logic is therefore usually assigned in the first place to the study of youth, who have not yet entered into the interests of concrete life, who live in leisure with a view to those interests, and who have first of all — for their subjective purpose — to occupy themselves with the acquisition of the means and of the possibility of becoming active in the objects of those interests — and with these themselves, still theoretically.

Among these means the logical science is counted, in defiance of the notion of Aristotle just cited; the occupation with it is a preliminary work, its place the school, upon which the seriousness of life and the activity for the true purposes are to follow.

In life the business is the use of the categories; they are degraded from the honour of being considered in themselves to serve in the spiritual business of living content, in the creating and the exchanging of the representations pertaining thereto — partly as abbreviations through their universality; for what an infinite multiplicity of details of external existence and activity does the representation: battle, war, people or sea, animal and the like hold together in itself; how is an infinite multiplicity of representations, activities, states and the like epitomized into the simplicity of such a representing, in the representation: God or love and the like! — partly for the closer determination and the discovery of the objective relations, in which, however, the content and the purpose, the correctness and the truth of the thinking which interferes are made wholly dependent on what is there, and no content-determining efficacy is ascribed to the determinations of thought in themselves.

Such a use of the categories, which has just been called the natural logic, is unconscious; and if in scientific reflection the relation of serving as means is imposed upon them in the mind, then thinking as such is made into something subordinated to the other spiritual determinations.

Of our feelings, drives and interests we do not readily say that they serve us, but they hold as independent forces and powers, so that we ourselves are this, so to feel, to desire and to will, to place this our interest in it.

But again, it can become more our consciousness that we stand in the service of our feelings, drives, passions and interests, and are in any case held by habit, than that we have them in our possession — still less that they, in our inner unity with them, serve us as means.

Determinations of this kind of sentiment and spirit show themselves to us now as particular in contrast to the universality of which we become conscious, in which we have our freedom, and we hold that we are rather captive in these particularities, that we are ruled by them.

Accordingly, we can hold even less that the forms of thought, which run through all our representations — be these merely theoretical or containing a material that belongs to feeling, to the drive, to the will — serve us, that we have them rather they us in our possession; what is left to us against them, how are we, I who set myself up as the more general over them, to place ourselves above them, they who are themselves the universal as such?

If we place ourselves in a feeling, a purpose, an interest and feel ourselves restricted and unfree therein, then the place into which we are able to retreat out of them and back into freedom is this place of the certainty of itself, of pure abstraction, of thinking.

Or again, if we want to speak of things, we call their nature or essence their concept, and this concept is only for thinking; but of the concepts of things we shall say even less that we master them or that the determinations of thought, of which they are the complex, serve us; on the contrary our thinking must be restricted by them, and our arbitrariness or freedom must not want to direct them after itself.

Insofar then as subjective thinking is our most own, most inward doing and the objective concept of things constitutes the thing itself, we cannot be outside that doing, cannot stand above it, and just as little can we get beyond the nature of things.

From the latter determination, however, we can abstain; it coincides with the former in so far as it would yield a relation of our thoughts to the thing, but something empty, because the thing would thereby be set up as the rule for our concepts, whereas the thing for us can be nothing other than our concepts of it.

If the critical philosophy understands the relation of these three termini in such a way that we place the thoughts between us and the things as the middle term, in the sense that this middle term rather separates us from the things instead of uniting us with them, then one must set against this view the simple observation that these very things, which are supposed to stand at the other extreme beyond us and beyond the thoughts which relate to them, are themselves thought-things and, being wholly undetermined, are only one thought-thing, — the so-called thing-in-itself of empty abstraction itself.
zh: 首先应当把这看作一个无限的进展：思维的形式从那种材料中被解放出来了，在这些材料里它们沉浸于自我意识的直观与表象，正如沉浸于我们的欲求与意愿，或者更确切地说沉浸于表象着的欲求与意愿（而没有表象，就不可能有人的欲求或意愿）；这些普遍性被为自身提升出来，并且如柏拉图首先、继而特别是亚里士多德所做的那样，被就其自身变成考察的对象；这就给出了对它们的认识的开始。「只有在几乎一切必需之物」亚里士多德说，「以及属于生活的便利与交往的东西都已经存在之后，人们才开始努力追求哲学的认识。」「在埃及，」他此前曾指出，「数学科学很早就得到了发展，因为那里的祭司阶层很早就被置于能够拥有闲暇的地位。」
——诚然，要从事纯粹思想的思考，需要预设人类精神必须走过的一段漫长历程；可以说，这是那个已经被满足的需要——对必然性的需要、对那必须达到的无所需要之需要——所产生的需要，是对撇开直观、想象等等之材料、撇开欲求与冲动与意志之具体利益的需要，而在这些材料中，思维规定正是包裹着藏着的。
在那种已经达到自身、只自在于自身的思维的静谧空间里，推动各民族与各个人生命的利益都沉默不语。「在这么多页之后，」亚里士多德在同样的关联中说，「人的本性是有依赖的；但这门不为任何用途而寻求的科学，唯独是自在自为自由的，因此它似乎并不是人的财产。」——哲学总体上仍然要在其思想中与具体的对象——上帝、自然、精神——打交道，但逻辑学只专注于这些对象在完整抽象中的自在自为。
因此，这门逻辑学通常首先成为青年的功课，因为这些青年还没有进入具体生活的利益，他们顾及着这些利益而在闲暇中生活，并且首先只是为了自己主观的目的，才不得不去获取手段以及在那些利益的客体上活动起来的可能性——从而对这些利益本身——还只是理论地——加以从事。
与亚里士多德上述的表象相抵触，逻辑科学被算作这些手段之一；对它的用力是一种预备性的工作，它的场所是学校，而生活的严肃以及对真实目的的活动的跟进，随后才应当到来。

在生活中，事情关乎范畴的运用；它们从被就其自身加以考察的荣誉上被降低下来，转而在有生命内容的精神运作中、在创造与更替相应表象的活动中效力——部分地是凭借其普遍性充当缩略词：因为「战斗」「战争」「民族或海洋」「动物」等等表象，把外在定在与活动的何等无尽的个别细节收拢在一起；而在「上帝或爱」等等表象中，又是如何把表象、活动、状态等等无尽的多种多样概括进这种表象活动的单纯性之中的！——部分地是为了更切近地规定与寻得对象的关系；但在这里，内容的充实与目的、掺入其中的思维的正确性与真理性，全都取决于现成的东西，而思维规定本身则不被赋予任何规定内容的效力。
这种范畴的运用——前面把它称作自然的逻辑学——是无意识的；而一旦在科学的反思中把「作为手段而效力」这一关系加在它们心上，那么思维本身就变成了从属于其他精神规定的东西。
对于我们的感受、冲动与利益，我们不会轻易说它们是为我们效力的；它们倒被看作独立的力量与势力，以至于我们自身就是这个：这样去感受、去欲求、去意愿，并把我们的利益置于此。
但同样地，比起我们拥有我们的感受、冲动、激情与利益，更能成为我们意识到的毋宁是：我们是处在对它们的服役之中，而且本来就受习惯支配；更不必说在我们与它们的内在统一中，它们是作为手段为我们效力了。
这类情感与精神的诸规定向我们显现出来，或者作为与那种我们据以意识到自身、并在其中拥有我们的自由普遍性相对立的特殊者；我们并认定，自己毋宁是被囚禁在这些特殊性之中，是被它们支配。
因此，我们就更不能认为，那些贯穿我们一切表象——无论这些表象只是理论的，还是包含着属于感受、冲动与意志的材料——的思维形式是在为我们效力；更不能说我们拥有它们、而非它们拥有我们；面对它们我们还剩下什么呢？我这个把自己设定为更普遍者的人，又怎能把自己置于它们之上呢——它们本身就是作为这样的普遍者。
当我们置身于某种感受、目的或利益之中，并在其中感到自己受限制、不自由时，我们能够从中脱出、退回到自由的那个场所，就是这个自身确定性的场所，就是纯粹抽象与思维的场所。
或者同样地，当我们要谈论事物时，我们把它们的自然或本质称作它们的概念，而这个概念只是为了思维而存在的；至于事物的概念，我们就更不能说我们掌握了它们，或者说构成它们之复合体的那些思维规定是为我们效力；相反，我们的思维必须受它们限制，而我们的任性或自由不应当想要按照自己的样子去支配它们。
那么，就主观思维是我们最属己、最内在的作为，而事物的客观概念就是事情本身而言，我们不能置身于那种作为之外，不能凌驾于其上；同样，我们也不能越出事物的本性。
不过，后一个规定我们可以不去管它；它与前一个规定重合，因为那只会给出我们的思想与事情之间的一种关系，但不过是空洞的，因为事情由此被立为我们的概念的法则，而事情对我们来说本来就只能是我们对它的概念。
如果批判哲学这样理解这三个项之间的关系：我们把思想置于我们与事情之间当作中项，其意义在于这个中项毋宁把我们与事情隔开，而不是把我们与它们联结起来，那么就得用一个简单的观察来反驳这种看法：这些恰恰应当站在另一极端、站在我们之外也站在那些以它们为对象的思想之外的事情，本身就是思想物，而且作为完全不确定的东西，它们只是一思想物——正是那种空洞抽象的所谓自在之物。

en: Yet this may suffice for the point of view from which the relation disappears, according to which the determinations of thought are taken only as for use and as a means; more important is what is further connected with this, according to which they are customarily conceived as external forms.

— The activity of thought which pervades all our representations, purposes, interests and actions is, as said, unconsciously busy (the natural logic); what our consciousness has before it is the content, the objects of the representations, that with which the interest is satisfied; according to this relation the determinations of thought hold as forms which are only at the content, and are not the content itself.

But if it is as has been indicated above and as is generally admitted, that nature, the peculiar essence, the truly permanent and substantial, is in the multiplicity and contingency of appearance and the transient expression the concept of the thing, the universal which is in it itself, like every human individual — indeed an infinitely peculiar one, which has in it the prius of all its peculiarity, of being man — just as every single animal has the prius of being an animal, then it would not be possible to say what such an individual would still be if this foundation were taken away from what is equipped with ever so many other predicates, nor whether, like the others, it could be called a predicate.

The indispensable foundation, the concept, the universal, the thought itself — insofar as one can abstract from the representation in the word "thought" — cannot be regarded merely as an indifferent form which is at some content.

But these thoughts of all natural and spiritual things, the substantial content itself, are still such a content as contains many determinations and still has in itself the difference between a soul and a body, between the concept and a relative reality; the deeper foundation is the soul for itself, the pure concept, which is the innermost of the objects, their simple pulse of life, as it is even of the subjective thinking of them.
To bring this logical nature, which animates the Spirit, drives and works in it, to consciousness — that is the task.

The instinctive action differs from the intelligent and free action in general by the fact that the latter happens with consciousness; when the content of the striving has been brought before the subject out of the immediate unity with it into objectivity, the freedom of the Spirit begins — the Spirit which in the instinctive working of thought, held fast in the bonds of its categories, is shattered into an infinitely manifold material.

In this net firmer knots are occasionally tied, which are the points of support and of direction of its life and consciousness; they owe their firmness and power precisely to the fact that they are, brought before consciousness, concepts of its essence which are in and for themselves.

The most important point for the nature of the Spirit is the relation not only of what it is in itself to what it actually is, but also of that as which it knows itself; this self-knowledge is, therefore, because it is essentially consciousness, the fundamental determination of its actuality.
The fundamental determination of its actuality.

To purify these categories, which are effective only instinctively as drives and are first brought into the consciousness of the Spirit individually, and with that mutably and confusingly, and so grant it an individual and uncertain actuality, and thereby to raise it in them to freedom and truth — this then is the higher logical task.
zh: 不过，对于那种使这一关系消失、按照它思维规定只被当作用途和手段来取用的观点，这也许就够了；更重要的是与此进一步相关的东西：按照它，思维规定通常被理解为外在的形式。
——贯穿我们一切表象、目的、利益与行动的思维活动，如前所述，是无意识地忙碌着的（自然的逻辑学）；我们的意识面前所有的是内容，是表象的对象，是那满足利益的东西；按这一关系，思维规定只作为附着于内容、而非内容本身的形式而成立。

但是，如果像前面所指出、并且通常为人所承认的那样：自然、那独特的本质、那真正持存而具实体性的东西，乃是在显现的多样性与偶然性以及转瞬即逝的表露之中，乃是事物的概念——那在自身之中的普遍者，就像每一个人类个体（他固然是一个无限独特的个体，其中人之为人的先在先于他的一切独特性）就像每一个单个动物含有着动物之为动物的先在一样——那么，如果把这个基础从那配备着无论多少其他谓词的东西那里拿走，就无法说出这样一个个体还该是什么，也无法说它是否像其他者一样还能被称作一个谓词。
那不可省略的基础——概念、普遍者、思想本身（就人能够从「思想」一词中的表象抽象出来而言）——不能仅仅被看作附着于某种内容的、漠不关心的形式。
但是，一切自然之物与精神之物的这些思想、连同那实体性的内容本身，仍然是这样的一个内容：它包含着多种多样的规定性，并且仍然在自身中带着灵魂与躯体、概念与相对实在性之间的差别；更深的基础则是自在的灵魂，是纯粹的概念——它是这些对象最内在的东西，是它们简单的生命脉搏，正如也是对它们的主观思维的生命脉搏。
把这逻辑本性——它赋予精神以生气，在精神中驱动并运作——带到意识中来，这就是任务。
本能性的作为与明智而自由的行为之所以有别，归根结底在于后者是带着意识发生的；当驱动着的东西的内容从与主体的直接统一中被带出来、成为对象性而置于主体面前时，精神的自由便开始了——这个精神在思维的本能性运作中，被束缚在它的范畴的锁链里，已经碎裂成无限多样的材料。
在这张网中不时会打起一些更结实的结点，它们是其生命与意识的支点与定向点；这些结点的牢固与力量恰恰在于：一旦被带到意识面前，它们就是其本质自在自为的概念。
对精神的本性来说最重要的点，是它自在之所是同它现实之所是之间的关系，而不只是它作为自己所知者的那个东西之间的关系；因为精神本质上就是意识，所以这种自我知识正是它现实性的基本规定。
它现实性的基本规定。
把这些仅仅本能地作为冲动而起作用的范畴——它们起初是单个地、因而可变而混乱地被带入精神的意识，并因此给精神一种孤立的、不确定的现实性——加以清洗，并借此把精神在它们之中提升到自由与真理，这就是更高的逻辑工作。

en: That we should take up, as the beginning of the science — whose high value in itself and at the same time as the condition of true cognition has just been acknowledged — the concepts and the moments of the concept in general, and treat the determinations of thought in the first place as forms which are different from the material and are only at it, this at once gives itself, in and for itself, to understand as an attitude inappropriate to the truth, which has been indicated as the object and purpose of logic.

For in so far as they are assumed merely as forms, as different from the content, they are taken up in a determination which stamps them as finite and makes them incapable of comprehending the truth, which is infinite in itself.

Be the true otherwise associated, in whatever respect, with limitation and finitude again — this is the side of its negation, of its untruth and unreality, precisely of its end, not the affirmation which it is as the true.

Against the baldness of the merely formal categories the instinct of healthy reason has finally felt itself so strengthened that it leaves their knowledge with contempt to the domain of a scholastic logic and scholastic metaphysics, together with the disregard of the value which the consciousness of these threads already has for itself, and with the unconsciousness of being held captive in the service of the unpurified and therefore unfree thinking — in the instinctive activity of the natural logic, still more in the reflective rejection of the knowledge and cognition of the determinations of thought themselves.

The single-threaded fundamental determination, or common formal determination, of the collection of such forms is identity, which is asserted in the logic of this collection as a law, as A = A, as Satz des Widerspruchs (law of contradiction).

Healthy reason has so completely lost its reverence before the school, which is in possession of such laws of truth and in which they are still always carried on, that it despises them for it and finds unbearable a man who knows how to speak truly according to such laws: "the plant is a — plant", "the science is — the science", and so on to infinity.

Regarding too the formulas which give the rules of inference — which is indeed a principal use of the understanding — there has established itself an equally justified consciousness: though it is unjust not to acknowledge that they have their field in cognition, in which they must hold, and at the same time that they are essential material for the thinking of reason, that they are at least indifferent means just as much of error and of sophistry, and, however else one may determine truth, are unusable for the higher truth, for example the religious truth, — that they concern in general only a correctness of cognitions, not truth.
zh: 我们把——作为科学的开端（它本身的高度价值以及它作为真正认识的条件刚刚已被承认）——概念以及概念的一般环节拿出来处理，把思维规定首先当作与材料不同、只附着于材料的形式来对待；这一点马上就自行表明：对于那被指认为逻辑学之对象与目的的真理来说，这是一个不恰当的举止。
因为一旦把它们只当作形式、当作与内容不同的东西来接受，它们就被纳入一种规定，这种规定把它们打上有限的印记，并使它们无力把握那在自身中无限的真理。
真实者本身无论从哪一方面看又怎样与限制和有限性结在一起——这都是它的否定、它的不真与不实在、正是它的终末这一面，而不是它作为真实者所是的那种肯定。
面对纯粹形式范畴的贫乏，健康理性的本能终于感到自己已足够强大：它怀着蔑视把对这些范畴的认识抛给经院逻辑学与经院形而上学这一领域，同时也丢掉了这些线头的意识本身已经具有的那份价值，以及那种不自觉——在自然的逻辑学的本能性作为中、在对思维规定本身之认识与认知的反思性拒斥中更是如此——把自己囚禁在未被清洗因而不自由的思维的奴役之中。
这一堆形式的单线的基本规定、或共同的形式规定，就是同一性；在这一堆形式的逻辑学里，它作为规律、作为 A = A、作为 Satz des Widerspruchs（矛盾律）而被主张。
健康理性已经把对那拥有这类真理法则、并且其中至今仍在继续推行的学派的敬意丧失殆尽，以至于它因此而蔑视这些法则，并且觉得一个懂得按照这类法则真实说话的人——「植物是——植物」「科学是——科学」，如此无穷无尽——是难以忍受的。
同样地，对于那些给出推论规则的公式——推论其实是知性的主要用途——也已经形成了这样一种同样正当的意识：不承认这些公式在认识中拥有其本应发挥作用的领域、不承认它们同时是理性思维的本质材料，是不公正的；但这些公式至少同样是错误与诡辩的漠不关心的手段，而且无论人们别样如何规定真理，它们对更高的真理（例如宗教的真理）都是不可用的；——总之它们所涉及的只是认识的正确性，而不是真理。

en: The incompleteness of this way of considering thought, which leaves truth on the side, can be supplemented only by the fact that not merely what is usually counted as external form, but the content as well, is drawn into the thinking contemplation.

It soon shows itself of its own accord that what in the most ordinary reflection is separated as content from form is indeed not meant to be formless and undetermined in itself — for then it would be only the empty, perhaps the abstraction of the thing-in-itself — but that it rather has form in itself, yes through it alone animation and content, and that it is form itself which turns over into the mere appearance of a content, and thereby also into the appearance of something external to this appearance.
With this introduction of the content into the logical contemplation, it is not the things but the thing, the concept of the things, which becomes the object.
Here, however, one can also be reminded that there are a multitude of concepts, a multitude of things.

What, however, limits this multitude has partly been said above: that the concept as thought in general, as the universal, is the immeasurable abbreviation as against the individuality of things as they float before the undetermined intuition and representation in their multitude; partly, however, a concept is in the first place the concept in itself, and this is only one and is the substantial foundation; but on the other hand it is indeed a determinate concept, and which determination it has in itself is that which appears as content; but the determinacy of the concept is a formal determination of this substantial unity, a moment of the form as totality, of the concept itself, which is the foundation of the determinate concepts.

This is not intuited or represented sensuously; it is only object, product and content of thinking and the thing in and for itself, the Logos, the reason of what is, the truth of what bears the name of things; least of all is the Logos that which is to be left outside the logical science.
It must therefore not be a matter of arbitrary choice whether to draw it into the science or to leave it outside.

If the determinations of thought, which are only external forms, are considered truly in themselves, then only their finitude and the untruth of their being-for-themselves can come to the fore, and, as their truth, the concept.

Hence the logical science, in so far as it treats the determinations of thought which traverse our Spirit instinctively and unconsciously and, even when they enter into language, remain objective-less and unnoticed, will also be the reconstruction of those which have been lifted out by reflection and fixed by it as subjective, external forms at the material and the content.
zh: 这种考察思维的方式所留下的不完整性——它把真理撇在了一边——只能这样来补足：不仅通常被算作外在形式的东西，而且内容本身，也被纳入思维着的考察之中。
很快就会自然显明：在最普通的反思中作为内容而与形式分开的东西，其实并不是要在自身中无形式、无规定——否则它就只是空洞的东西，比如自在之物的抽象——毋宁说它在自身中就有形式，甚至唯有通过形式才获得生气与充实；而正是形式本身才转变为仅仅内容的一个假象，因而也转变为这个假象之外者的一个假象。
随着内容被引入逻辑的考察，成为对象的就不是那些事物，而是事情，是事物的概念。
不过在这里也可以提醒人们：有许多多的概念，有许多多的事情。

但究竟是什么限制了这众多之物，一方面前面已经说过：概念作为思想本身、作为普遍者，是与事物的个别性相对的无量缩略词——这些事物在它们众多之中漂浮于不确定的直观与表象之前；另一方面，概念首先自在地就是概念本身，而这个自在的概念只有一个，它就是实体性的基础；但另一方面，它又确实是一个具体的概念，它在自身所具有的那种规定性，就是显现为内容的东西；而概念的规定性则是这一实体性统一的一个形式规定，是形式作为总体性的一个环节，是概念本身的环节——概念本身乃是那些具体概念的基础。
它不是被感性地直观或表象的；它只是思维的对象、产品与内容，是自在自为的事情，是 Logos（逻各斯），是存在者的理性，是那些带着事物之名的者的真理；最不该被留在逻辑科学之外的，恰恰是 Logos。
因此，是否把它拉进这门科学、或把它留在外面，都不能听凭随意。
如果那些不过是外在形式的思维规定真正在自身上被考察，那么能显露出来的就只有它们的有限性、它们「应当自为」这一要求的不真实性，以及作为它们的真理的概念。
因此，逻辑科学在处理那些总体上本能地、无意识地贯穿我们精神的思维规定——即便它们进入语言，也仍然无对象、不受注意——的同时，也将是那些被反思提升出来、并被反思固定为主体性的、外在于材料与充实的形式的思维规定的重建。

en: The exposition of no object would in itself be capable of being so strictly and entirely immanently plastic as the exposition of the development of thought in its necessity; none carries this demand with it so strongly; its science would in this also have to surpass mathematics, for no object has in itself this freedom and independence.

Such an exposition would require, as this is present in its own way in the course of mathematical consequence, that at no stage of the development there occur a determination of thought and a reflection which do not emerge immediately in this stage and are not carried over into it from the preceding ones.

Of such abstract perfection of the exposition, however, one must generally renounce; already, since the science must begin with the purely simple, and hence with the most universal and emptiest, the exposition would allow only these quite simple expressions of the simple themselves, without any further addition of any word; — what would be permissible in respect of the matter would be negative reflections which endeavour to hold off and remove what the representation or an unregulated thinking might otherwise mix in.

Such reflections in the simple immanent course of the development are, however, due in themselves; and the endeavour to ward them off is thus itself afflicted with this contingency; in any case it is in vain to want to encounter all such reflections precisely because they lie outside the matter, and at least it would be incompleteness that would be demanded here for systematic satisfaction.
But the peculiar restlessness and dispersion of our modern consciousness allows nothing else than to take more or less account as well of obvious reflections and ideas.

A plastic exposition then also requires a plastic sense for receiving and understanding; but such plastic youths and men, so quietly with the self-renunciation of their own reflections and ideas, with which the thinking for itself impatiently proves itself, listeners who follow only the matter, as Plato sings, could not be exhibited in a modern dialogue; still less could such readers be counted upon.

On the contrary, opponents have shown themselves to me far too often and far too eagerly, who were unwilling to make the simple reflection that their ideas and objections contain categories which are assumptions and themselves first require criticism before they can be used.

The unconsciousness about this goes incredibly far; it produces the fundamental misunderstanding, the bad, i.e. uncultivated behaviour of thinking something else when a category which is being considered is in question, and not this category itself.

This unconsciousness is all the less to be justified, since such an other consists in other determinations of thought and concepts, whereas in a system of logic these other categories too must have found their place and there too must have been subjected to consideration in themselves.

This is most striking in the overwhelming multitude of objections and attacks on the first concepts or propositions of logic, being and nothing and becoming, in which becoming, itself a simple determination, is undisputed — the simplest analysis shows this — as containing those two determinations as moments.

Thoroughness seems to require that the beginning, as the ground on which everything is built, be investigated before everything else, indeed that one proceed no further than until it has proved itself firmly, and rather, on the contrary, if this is not the case, to reject everything that follows.

This thoroughness has at the same time the advantage of granting the greatest relief to the work of thinking; it has the whole development enclosed in this germ before it and considers itself finished with everything when it is finished with this, which is the easiest thing to dispose of, for it is the simplest, the single-threaded itself; it is the little labour that is required which essentially recommends this so self-satisfied thoroughness.
This restriction to the simple leaves the arbitrary of thinking, which does not want to remain simple by itself but rather brings its reflections about it into play, free scope.

With the good right of occupying itself first with the principle alone and thereby not engaging with what is further, this thoroughness in its own work does the opposite of this; rather it brings in what is further, i.e. other categories than the principle alone, other assumptions and prejudices.

Such assumptions — that infinity is different from finitude, that the content is something other than the form, that the inner is other than the outer, that mediation is likewise not immediacy — as though anyone did not know such things, are at the same time brought forward in the manner of instruction, and are told and assured rather than proved.

In such instructing as behaviour there lies — one cannot call it otherwise — a silliness; in respect of the matter, partly the unwarrantedness of merely assuming such things and positively taking them for granted, but partly and still more the ignorance that it is the need and business of logical thinking precisely to investigate whether such a finite thing without infinity is anything true, whether likewise such an abstract infinity, further a formless content and a contentless form, an inner for itself which has no expression, an externality without internality and so on, is anything true, likewise anything actual.

— But this formation and discipline of thought, through which a plastic comportment of it is to be brought about and the impatience of obtruding reflection overcome, is procured only by going further, by the study and the production of the whole development.
zh: 没有任何对象的表述本身能像思维在其必然性中的发展之表述那样，严格而完全内在地具有可塑性；没有任何对象如此强烈地带有这一要求；它的科学在这方面甚至必须超越数学，因为没有任何对象在自身中具有这样的自由与独立性。
这样的表述要求——正如在数学推论的进程中所存在的那样——发展的任何一个阶段上都不出现这样一种思维规定与反思：它不是在这一阶段中直接产生，并且不是从先前的阶段里转移到这一阶段里来的。
不过，对表述的这种抽象完善性，一般说来是必须放弃的；因为科学一开始就得从纯粹单纯的东西、因而从最普遍而最空的东西开始，那么这种表述就只能容许这些关于单纯者的、十分单纯的表达，不许再加任何一个字；——就事情本身而言可以有的，只是一些否定性的反思，它们设法挡住并清除表象或一种不受规训的思维否则会掺入的东西。
然而，这类想法在发展的单纯内在进程中是必然要产生的；因而，设法挡住它们的努力本身也就带上了这种偶然性；况且，想要抵挡所有这类想法本身就是徒劳的——恰恰因为它们处在事情之外；而在这里，为了体系上的满足所要求的，至少会是不完全性。
但我们现代意识特有的不安与涣散，使人不至于别的做法，只能同样或多或少地顾及那些浅显的反思与想法。
一种可塑性的表述于是也要求有一种可塑性的接受与理解的能力；然而这样一些可塑性的青年与人士——他们以对自身反思与想法的自我否认而如此安静，而那种独自的思维却不耐烦地要以此证明自己——像柏拉图所歌咏的那样只跟随事情本身的听者，在现代的对话中是不可能被安排出来的；就更不必指望这样的读者了。
恰恰相反，这样一些对手在我面前出现得过于频繁、过于急切：他们不愿作那个简单的反思——即他们的想法与反驳所包含的范畴乃是一些前提，而这些前提本身在被使用之前首先还需要批判。
对此的无知走得远得难以置信；它造成一种根本的误解、一种恶劣的即没有教养的举止：在考察一个范畴时去想别的东西，而不是想这个范畴本身。
这种无知就更难辩护，因为这样的「别的」乃是另一些思维规定与概念，而在逻辑学的体系中，恰恰这些别的范畴同样必须找到自己的位置，并且在那里同样必须就其自身受到考察。
这一点在大量针对逻辑学最初概念或命题——存在与无与生成——的反驳与攻击中最为触目：生成本身就是一个简单的规定，这一点大概无人争议——最简单的分析就表明了这一点——因为它把那两个规定作为自己的环节包含着。
严谨似乎要求：把开端——一切所建造于其上的根据——放在一切之前加以考察，甚至不得走得比「它已被确凿地证明」更远；相反，若情形并非如此，就要把随后的一切都抛掉。
这种严谨同时还有一个好处：它为思维的工作提供最大的轻松；它把整个发展收拢在这一个萌芽之中置于自己面前，并且当它与这个萌芽了结时，就认为自己与一切都已了结——而这个萌芽是最容易了结的，因为它本身就是最单纯的东西、那单线的东西本身；正是在于所需工作量之微小，这种如此自满的严谨才真正值得推荐。
这种对单纯者的限制，给了思维的任性以自由活动的余地——思维不甘心自己就停留在单纯上，反而要把关于它的反思施展出来。
它正当地只先与原则打交道、因而并不牵涉更进一步的东西；然而这种严谨在自己的工作中所做的恰恰与此相反：它反而把更进一步的东西、即原则之外的另一些范畴、另一些前提与偏见搬了进来。
这样一些前提——无限不同于有限、内容是不同于形式的某种东西、内在不同于外在、中介同样不是直接性——仿佛有人不知道这类事情似的，同时又以说教的方式被提出来；它们不是被证明的，而是被讲述与断言的。

在这样以说教的方式行事之中蕴藏着——不能换个说法——一种愚蠢；就事情本身而言，一半在于只是预设这类东西、径直把它们当作理所当然的无正当性，另一半则更在于无知：逻辑思维的需要与工作恰恰就是去考察：这样一个没有无限性的有限者是否真有任何真实的东西，同样，这样一种抽象的无限性，乃至一个无形式的内容与一个无内容的形式，一个自在而没有外在表现的内在，一个没有内在性的外在性等等，是否真有任何真实的东西、同样有任何现实的东西。
——但是，思维的这种陶冶与规训——通过它可以造成思维的可塑性举止，并克服那种突发的反思所带的不耐烦——只有靠继续前进、靠对整个发展的研习与生产才能获得。

en: At the mention of Platonic exposition, whoever labours to erect anew in modern times an independent edifice of philosophical science may be reminded of the story that Plato reworked his books on the State seven times.

The reminder of this, a comparison, insofar as it seemed to contain one in itself, would only all the more drive to the wish that for a work which, as belonging to the modern world, has before it a deeper principle, a heavier subject and a material of richer compass to be worked up, the free leisure to work through it seventy-seven times had been granted.

Yet the author, considering it in the face of the greatness of the task, had to content himself with what it might have become, under the circumstances of an external necessity, of the unavoidable dispersion through the greatness and many-sidedness of the interests of the time, even under the doubt whether the loud noise of the day and the stupefying garrulity of the imagination, which is vainly eager to confine itself to the same, still leave room open for a share in the passionless stillness of cognition which only thinks.
zh: 在提到柏拉图式的表述时，凡在现代致力于重新建造一座哲学科学的独立大厦的人，都会被提醒那个说法：柏拉图曾七次重写他关于《国家篇》的著作。
对此的提醒——这一比较，只要它似乎本身包含着一项比较——只会更加驱使人去希望：对于这样一部作品——它作为属于现代世界的作品，面前有一个更深的原理、一个更沉重的主题和一份范围更为丰富的材料可供加工——那把它通读七十七遍的自由闲暇当初若是获准了该有多好。
而作者面对任务的巨大，只能满足于它可能成为的样子：处在一种外在的必然性之下，处在因时代利益之巨大与多方面性而来的、无法避免的涣散之下，甚至处在这样的疑虑之下：白日的喧闹与想象那种令人昏昏然的喋喋不休——想象徒然急切地要把自身局限在同一事物上——是否还会给那种仅仅思考的、无激情的认识之静谧留出可以分享的余地。

en: Berlin, 7 November 1831
Nowhere is the need to begin from the thing itself, without preceding reflections, felt more strongly than in the logical science.

In every other science the subject which it treats and the scientific method are distinguished from one another; just as the content too does not make an absolute beginning but depends on other concepts and is connected around itself with other material.

To these sciences it is therefore granted to speak of their ground and its connections as well as of the method only in the manner of lemmas, to apply without further ado the forms of definitions and the like which are presupposed as known and assumed, and to make use of the ordinary kind of ratiocination for the fixing of their general concepts and fundamental determinations.
zh: 在任何一门科学中，像在逻辑科学中那样强烈地感觉到这样的需要：不作事前的反思，直接从事情本身开始。
在别的每一门学问中，它所处理的对象与科学的方法都是彼此分开的；其内容同样并不构成一个绝对的起点，而是依赖别的概念，并在自己周围与别的材料联结着。
因此，这些科学被允许的，只是以命题式的方式谈论它们的根据及其关联以及方法，无须多言地运用那些被预设为已知与已被假定的定义之类形式，并使用通常的推理方式，来确定它们的一般概念与基本规定。

en: Logic, on the contrary, cannot presuppose any of these forms of reflection or rules and laws of thought, for they themselves form a part of its content and first have to be grounded within it.

Not only the statement of the scientific method but also the concept of science itself belongs to its content, and indeed it constitutes its final result; what it is, therefore, it cannot announce in advance, but its whole treatise first brings forth this knowledge of itself as its last thing and as its completion.
Likewise its subject, thought or more precisely comprehending thought, is essentially treated within it; the concept of it generates itself in its course and thus cannot be sent ahead.

What is therefore sent ahead in this Introduction has not the purpose of grounding the concept of logic or of justifying in advance, scientifically, the content and the method of the same, but rather of bringing closer to the representation, through a few explanations and reflections in a ratiocinative and historical sense, the point of view from which this science is to be considered.
zh: 逻辑学则相反：它不能预设这些反思形式或思维的规则与法则中的任何一种，因为它们本身就构成其内容的一部分，并且首先必须在它里面得到奠基。
不仅科学方法的说明，而且科学这个概念本身也属于它的内容；而且它构成逻辑学最后的结果；因此，逻辑学是什么，它不能预先宣告，而是它的全部论述才把这关于自身的知识作为它的最后之物、作为它的完成首先呈现出来。
同样，它的对象——思维，或更确切地说，以概念把握的思维——也主要是在它里面得到处理的；关于它的概念在它的进程中自行产生出来，因而不能预先被派在前面。
因此在这篇导言中被预先提出的东西，其目的并不是要奠定逻辑学这个概念，或先在地从科学上为逻辑学的内容与方法作辩护，而是要通过若干解释与在推理和历史意义上的反思，把应当据以考察这门科学的那个立场更接近于表象。

en: When logic is taken in general as the science of thought, it is understood at the same time that this thought constitutes merely the form of a cognition, that logic abstracts from all content and that the so-called second component which belongs to a cognition, the matter, has to be given from elsewhere; that thus logic, being entirely independent of this matter, can only state the formal conditions of true cognition, but cannot itself contain real truth, nor even be the path to real truth, because precisely the essential of truth, the content, lies outside it.
zh: 如果人们通常把逻辑学当作一般意义上的思维科学来接受，那么与此同时也就以为：这种思维只构成一种认识的形式，以为逻辑学撇开一切内容，以为所谓属于认识的第二个组成部分、即「物质」，必须从别处给予；于是人们以为：逻辑学既然完全与这种物质无关，就只能陈述真正的认识的形式条件，却既不能包含实在的真理本身，也不能成为通往实在的真理的道路，因为真理的本质即内容恰恰在它之外。

en: In the first place, however, it is already clumsy to say that logic abstracts from all content, that it teaches only the rules of thought without being able to enter into what is thought and to take its character into account.

For since thinking and the rules of thought are to be its object, it has immediately in them its peculiar content; it has in them too that second component of cognition, a matter, whose character it cares about.
zh: 首先，说逻辑学撇开一切内容、说它只教思维的规则而不能进入所思想者并顾及它的性质，这就已经是笨拙的了。
因为既然思维与思维的规则应当是它的对象，那么它就直接地在其中有自己特有的内容；它在其中也有认识的第二个组成部分、一种物质，并且关心这种物质的性质。

en: But in the second place, the representations on which the concept of logic has hitherto rested have partly already perished, and partly it is time that they should disappear completely, that the standpoint of this science should be conceived more highly, and that it should gain a completely changed shape.
zh: 但其次，逻辑学这个概念迄今所依托的那些表象，一部分已经消失了，另一部分则到了该让它们彻底消失的时候了：该把这门科学的立场设想得更高，并且使它获得一种完全改变了的形态。

en: The concept of logic hitherto rests on the separation, presupposed once and for all in ordinary consciousness, of the content of cognition and its form, or of truth and certainty.

First it is presupposed that the material of cognition exists in itself as a finished world outside thought, that thought is empty in itself, that it enters externally as a form upon that matter, fills itself with it, first gains a content in it and thereby becomes a real cognition.
zh: 逻辑学迄今的概念，建立在普通意识一次性预设的区分之上，即把认识的内容与它的形式分开，或者把真理与确定性分开。
首先是预设：认识的材料作为一个现成的世界自在地存在于思维之外；思维自在地是空的；它作为一种形式从外面趋近那种物质，并由此充满自身，首先在其中获得一个内容，并由此成为实在的认识。

en: Then these two components (for they are to have the relation of components, and cognition is to be composed from them mechanically or at the most chemically) stand toward each other in this order of rank: that the object is something in itself complete and finished which can do entirely without thought for its actuality, and conversely that thought is something defective which first has to complete itself at some material, and indeed as a soft indeterminate form has to accommodate itself to its matter.
Truth is the agreement of thought with the object, and in order to bring about this agreement — for it does not exist in itself — thought is to accommodate and adjust itself to the object.
zh: 其次，这两个组成部分（因为它们应当具有组成部分之间的关系，而认识将由它们机械地、或至多化学地组合而成）彼此之间是这样一种等级次序：客体是一个自在地完美、现成的东西，可以完全不需要思维而具有它的现实性；反过来，思维则是某种有缺陷的东西，它首先得在某种材料上才得以完成，而且还得作为一种柔软而不确定的形式去迁就它的物质。
真理是思维与对象的一致；而为了产生这种一致——因为一致并不是自在地存在的——思维就应当顺从对象、迁就对象。

en: Thirdly, in so far as the diversity of matter and form, of object and thought, is not left in that misty indeterminacy but taken more determinately, each is a sphere separated from the other.

Thought therefore does not in its receiving and forming of the material get beyond itself; its receiving and its accommodation to the material remains a modification of itself; it does not thereby become its other; and the self-conscious determining belongs anyway only to it; thus even in its relation to the object it does not go out of itself to the object: the object remains as a thing in itself quite simply a beyond of thought.
zh: 第三，如果物质与形式、对象与思维之间的相异不是被留在那种雾蒙蒙的不确定性里，而是被更确定地把握，那么两者各自就是一个与对方分开的领域。
因此，思维在接收并塑造材料时并没有越出自身；它的接收与对材料的迁就仍然是它自身的某种样态，它并不因此变成自己的他者；而那种自我意识的规定原本就只属于它；所以即使在与对象的关系中，它也不是从自身走出去走向对象：对象作为自在之物干脆就是思维的一个彼岸。

en: These views about the relation of subject and object to each other express the determinations which constitute the nature of our ordinary, appearing consciousness; but these prejudices, transferred to reason as if the same relation obtained in it, as if this relation had truth in and for itself, are the errors whose refutation carried through all parts of the spiritual and natural universe is the philosophy — or rather, since they block the entrance to philosophy, they are to be set aside before it.
zh: 这些关于主体与客体彼此关系的看法，表达出构成我们普通的、显现的意识之性质的那些规定；但这些偏见一旦被转移到理性上，仿佛在理性中也有同样的关系、仿佛这一关系自在地具有真理，那么它们就是那些错误——而哲学正是对它们在精神宇宙与自然宇宙的所有部分中所作的反驳；或者更确切地说，因为它们挡在哲学的入口上，所以必须在哲学面前把它们搁在一旁。

en: The older metaphysics had in this respect a higher conception of thinking than has come into fashion in more recent times.

That one, namely, took as its foundation that what is recognized of and through things by thinking is the only thing truly true in them, thus not the things in their immediacy but the things first raised into the form of thought, as thought-things.

This metaphysics thus held that thinking and the determinations of thought are not something foreign to the objects but rather their essence, or that things and thinking of them (as our language too expresses an affinity of the two) agree in and for themselves, that thinking in its immanent determinations and the true nature of things are one and the same content.
zh: 在这点上，较早的形而上学对思维有一个比近代通行的那种更高的概念。
因为它所预设的是：通过思维从事物上并由思维所认识到的那个东西，才是它们身上唯一真正真实的东西；因此，不是事物在其直接性上，而是事物被提升到思维的形式中、作为被思想者，才是这样的真者。
这种形而上学因此认为：思维以及思维的规定并不是对对象而言陌生的东西，而毋宁就是对象的本质；或者说，事物与对事物的思维（正如我们的语言也表达出二者之间的亲缘一样）自在地是一致的，思维在其内在规定中与事物的真实本性乃是同一个内容。

en: But the reflecting understanding took possession of philosophy.

It is worth knowing precisely what this expression is meant to say, which is otherwise often used as a slogan; what is meant by it is generally the abstracting and thereby dividing understanding, which persists in its separations.

Turned against reason, it behaves as the common sense of ordinary men and maintains its view that truth rests on sensuous reality, that thoughts are only thoughts in the sense that only sensuous perception gives them content and reality, that reason, in so far as it remains in and for itself, engenders nothing but brain-spun phantasms.

In this turning away of reason from itself the concept of truth is lost; it is restricted to recognizing only subjective truth, only the appearance, only something which does not correspond to the nature of the thing itself; knowledge has fallen back to opinion.
zh: 但反思的知性攫取了哲学。
这个说法（它平时常被当作口号使用）究竟意指什么，是值得确切知道的；它一般所指的乃是那种抽象、因而也就是分割的知性，它坚持于自己的种种分割。
一旦掉转过来反对理性，它就以常人的常识行事，并坚持自己的看法：真理建立在感性的实在性上；思想终究只是思想，因为唯有感性的知觉才赋予它们充实与实在性；理性只要自在地保持自身，就只会生出头脑的幻影。
在理性这样撇开自身的情形中，真理的概念丧失了；它被限缩为只认识主观的真理、只认识现象、只认识某种与事情本身的本性不相符合的东西；知识退回到了意见。

en: This turn, however, which recognition takes and which appears as loss and retrogression, has at its foundation the deeper thing on which the elevation of reason into the higher spirit of modern philosophy rests in general.
The ground of that notion which has become general is namely to be sought in the insight into the necessary conflict of the determinations of the understanding with themselves.
— The reflection already named is this: to go beyond the concrete immediacy and to determine and separate the same.
But it must just as much go beyond these its separating determinations and first relate itself to them.
On the standpoint of this relating, the conflict of those determinations comes to light.

This relating of reflection belongs in itself to reason; the elevation above those determinations which arrives at the insight into their conflict is the great negative step towards the true concept of reason.

But the insight which is not carried out falls into the misunderstanding, as if it were reason which comes into conflict with itself; it does not recognize that the conflict is precisely the elevation of reason above the restrictions of the understanding and the dissolution of these.

Instead of making the last step upward from here, the cognition has flowed back from the unsatisfactoriness of the determinations of the understanding to sensuous existence, presuming to have the firm and the one there.

But in so far as, on the other side, this cognition knows itself to be the cognition of what merely appears, the unsatisfactoriness of it is admitted, but at the same time presupposed, as if although not the things in themselves, yet within the sphere of appearance things would be recognized correctly, as if in this the kind of objects were merely different and the one kind, namely the things in themselves, not indeed, but the other kind, namely the appearances, would fall into cognition.
As if a correct insight were attributed to a man with the addition that he is capable of insight into nothing true but only into the untrue.
As absurd as the latter is, so absurd is a true cognition which did not recognize the object as it is in itself.
zh: 然而，认识所采取的、看上去像是损失与倒退的这一转向，其基础乃是那更深的东西——近代哲学中理性向更高精神的提升，总体上就建立在它之上。
那个已成为通行表象的根基，须在「洞见知性的诸规定与自身的必然抵触」之中去寻找。
——前面已经点明的那种反思就是：越过具体的直接性，去规定它并把它分开。
但它同样必须越过这些分割性的规定，并首先与它们建立起关系。
在建立这种关系的立场上，这些规定的抵触就显现出来了。
反思的这种「建立关系」自在地属于理性；而超越那些规定、从而达到对它们抵触的洞见，乃是通向理性真概念的那个伟大的否定步骤。
但那未被贯彻的洞见陷入了误解，以为是理性本身与自身相抵触；它没有认识到：矛盾恰恰就是理性对知性之限制的提升以及对那些限制的消解。
认识非但没有从这里再向上迈出最后一步，反而从知性诸规定的不满足那里退流回感性的存在，以为在那里就能占有那坚固者与那唯一者。
但在另一方面，这种认识知道自己只是关于显现者的认识时，它的不满足就被承认了；与此同时却又预设：仿佛虽不是自在之物、但至少在现象的范围内事物会被正确地认识；仿佛这不过是对象的种类不同，而那一种、即自在之物固然不会落入认识，但那另一种、即现象，却会落入认识。
这就像给一个人加上一句附注，说他虽有正确洞见，却只能够洞见不真者而非真者。
后者是何等荒谬，一个不把对象当作自在之物来认识的真实认识就是何等荒谬。

en: The criticism of the forms of the understanding has had the result indicated above, that these forms have no application to the things in themselves.
— This can have no other meaning than that these forms are in themselves something untrue.

But in so far as they are left to hold for subjective reason and for experience, the criticism has brought about no change in them themselves, but leaves them for the subject in the same shape in which they otherwise held for the object.
But if they are inadequate for the thing in itself, then the understanding, to which they are supposed to belong, would have to be even less willing to approve of them and to be content with them.
If they cannot be determinations of the thing in itself, they can still less be determinations of the understanding, to which at least the dignity of a thing in itself ought to be granted.

The determinations of the finite and the infinite are in the same conflict, whether they be applied to time and space, to the world, or whether they be determinations within the spirit, — just as well as black and white make a grey, whether they are combined with one another on a wall or still on the palette.

If our world-picture dissolves, in that the determinations of the infinite and the finite are transferred onto it, then even more the Spirit itself, which contains both in itself, is a self-contradictory, a self-dissolving one.

— It is not the character of the material or object, on which they would be applied or in which they are located, that can make a difference; for the object has the contradiction on it only through and in accordance with those determinations.
zh: 对知性诸形式的批判所得出的结果如前所述：这些形式对自在之物不适用。
——这不可能有别的意思，只能是说：这些形式自在地是某种不真的东西。
但只要它们仍被留作对主观理性与对经验有效，批判就没有在它们自身上造成任何改变，而是把它们为主体保留在它们原本对客体有效的那种形态里。
但如果它们对自在之物尚且不足，那么那个它们本应归属的知性，就更应当不情愿接受它们、更不情愿以它们为满足。
如果它们不能是自在之物的规定，那么它们就更不能是知性的规定——因为至少还应当承认知性有自在之物的尊严。
有限者与无限者的诸规定处在同一种抵触之中：无论它们被应用于时间与空间、应用于世界，还是它们是精神内部的诸规定；——正如黑与白调出灰色来，无论它们是在墙上相混，还是还留在调色板上。
如果我们的世界表象在无限者与有限者的诸规定被转移到它上面时解消了，那么更其如此：那个在自身中包含着二者的精神，本身就是一个自相矛盾的、一个自我消解的东西。
——能够造成差别的并不是它们所被应用其上、或它们所处其中的材料或对象的性质；因为对象身上的矛盾，只是通过并按照那些规定才有的。

en: That criticism has thus only removed the forms of objective thinking from the thing, but left them in the subject as it found them.

For in doing so it did not consider these forms in and for themselves, according to their peculiar content, but simply took them over as lemmas from subjective logic; so that there was no question of a derivation of them in themselves, nor of a derivation of them as subjective-logical forms, still less of the dialectical consideration of them.
zh: 所以那种批判只是把客观思维的形式从事物那里移开了，却把它们在主体中原样留下。
因为它这样做时，并不是就这些形式自在地、按照它们特有的内容来考察它们，而是径直从主观逻辑学把它们当作命题接受下来；因此，既谈不上从它们自身出发对它们的演绎，也谈不上把它们作为主观逻辑形式的演绎，更谈不上对它们的辩证考察。

en: The consistently carried-through transcendental idealism has recognized the nullity of the specter of the thing-in-itself still left over by critical philosophy, this abstract shadow separated from all content, and has had the purpose of destroying it completely.
This philosophy also made the beginning of letting reason present its determinations from itself.
But the subjective attitude of this attempt prevented it from coming to completion.
Further, this attitude, and with it that beginning and the development of pure science, have been abandoned.
zh: 一以贯之的先验观念论看出了批判哲学所遗留下来的自在之物这个幽灵——这个与一切内容相分离的抽象影子——的空无，并且其目的就是把它彻底摧毁。
这门哲学也开创了让理性从自身出发展示自己的规定。
但这一尝试的主观立场使它未能达到完成。
此外，这一立场以及随之而来的那个开端与纯粹科学的展开，也都已被放弃了。

en: Quite without regard to metaphysical meaning, however, what is commonly understood by logic is considered.
This science, in the state in which it still finds itself, has indeed no content of the kind that holds in ordinary consciousness as reality and as a true thing.
But it is not on this account a formal science lacking contentful truth.
In that material which is missed in it, to whose lack the unsatisfactoriness of this science is habitually ascribed, the domain of truth is in any case not to be sought.
Rather, the want of content in the logical forms lies solely in the manner in which they are considered and treated.
In that they fall apart as fixed determinations and are not held together in an organic unity, they are dead forms and do not have the Spirit in them, which is their living concrete unity.
But in that they thereby lack a substantial content, — a matter which would be content in itself.

The content which is missed in the logical forms is nothing other than a firm foundation and concretion of these abstract determinations; and such a substantial essence is habitually sought for them outside.
But the logical reason itself is the substantial or real which holds all abstract determinations together in itself and is their substantial, absolutely concrete unity.

Thus, according to what is habitually called matter, one need not look far; it is not the fault of the object of logic if it is to be without content, but solely that of the way in which the same is conceived.
zh: 不过，这里所考察的完全是不问形而上学意义、通常被理解为逻辑学的东西。
这门科学就它目前所处的状态而言，当然没有那种在普通意识中被视为实在性、被视为真实事情的内容。
但它并不因此就是一门形式的、缺少内容充实的真理的科学。
在那于它里面被缺少的材料之中——人们通常把它的那种不满足归咎于这一缺少——本来就不该去寻找真理的领域。
毋宁说，逻辑形式的无内容单单在于考察和处理它们的方式。
由于它们作为固定的规定而散开、没有被在一个有机的统一中维系起来，它们就是死形式，其中并没有精神居住——精神正是它们活生生的具体统一。
但这样一来，它们就缺少那种扎实的内容——一种自身即有充实的物质。
在逻辑形式上被缺少的内容，无非就是这些抽象规定的一个坚固基础与具体性；而这样的一种实体性的本质，人们通常要在它们之外去寻找。
但逻辑理性本身就是那个把一切抽象规定保持于自身之中的实体者或实在者，并且是它们扎实的、绝对具体的统一。
因此，就通常被称作「物质」的东西而言，本来不必费心去寻找；若逻辑学的内容贫乏，那并不是逻辑学对象的过错，而完全在于对这个对象的把握方式。

en: This reflection leads more precisely to the statement of the standpoint according to which logic is to be considered, in how far it differs from the previous mode of treatment of this science and is the only true standpoint on which it is henceforth forever to be established.
zh: 这一反思更进而指向那个立场的说明：逻辑学应当依照这个立场来考察；这个立场与这门科学迄今的处理方式有何不同，以及它何以是唯一真实的立场、逻辑学今后应当永远建立在它之上。

en: In the Phenomenology of Spirit I have presented consciousness in its onward movement from the first immediate opposition between itself and the object up to absolute knowledge.
This path passes through all the forms of the relation of consciousness to the object and has the concept of science as its result.

This concept therefore (apart from the fact that it emerges within logic itself) requires here no justification, because it has received it there; and it is capable of no other justification than just this production of it by consciousness, in which all its own shapes resolve themselves into it as into truth.

— A ratiocinative grounding or explanation of the concept of science can at most achieve that it is brought before the representation and that a historical knowledge of it is brought about; but a definition of science, or more precisely of logic, has its proof solely in that necessity of its coming into being.

A definition with which any science makes the absolute beginning can contain nothing other than the determinate and regular expression of that which one admittedly and commonly presupposes under the object and purpose of the science.

That one should conceive precisely this under it is a historical assurance, with respect to which one can only appeal to this and that recognized, or properly only request in a suppliant manner that this and that be allowed to count as recognized.

It never ceases that the one brings forward a case and an instance from here, the other from there, according to which still something more and different is to be understood in this and that expression, into whose definition therefore a more determinate or more general determination is still to be taken up, and according to which the science too is to be established.

— Moreover, it depends on reasoning what all and to what limit and extent it must draw in or exclude; but to reasoning itself the most diverse and varied opinions are open, over which at the end only arbitrariness can conclude a fixed determination.
In this procedure of beginning the science with its definition, the need is not at issue that the necessity of its object and thereby of itself should be demonstrated.
zh: 在《精神现象学》中，我呈现了意识从它与对象的第一个直接对立、直到绝对知识的推进过程。
这条道路穿过意识与客体关系的一切形态，并以科学的概念为其结果。
因此，这个概念（姑且不论它是在逻辑学内部自身产生出来的）在这里不需要任何辩护，因为它在那里已经得到了辩护；而它除了意识对它的这一产生之外，也不容许有任何别的辩护——在意识的这一产生中，它自己的种种形态全都解消为它、解消为真理。
——对科学概念的推理性论证或解释，最多只能做到：把它带到表象面前，并由此造成对它的历史性认识；但科学——更确切地说逻辑学——的定义，其证明只在于它产生的那个必然性。
任何一门科学用来作绝对开端的那个定义，所能包含的无非是：人们公认且通常预设的关于该科学的对象与目的的那个东西的规定性、规范的表达。
至于人们恰好是在这个概念之下设想所说的东西，那是一种历史上的担保；就它而言，人们只能援引这个那个已被承认的东西，或者严格说来只能以请求的方式提出：请让这个那个被当作已被承认的。
这从来不会停止：一个人从这里、另一个人从那里提出一个案例与实例；据此，在这个那个表述之下还应当理解更多别的东西，因而在它的定义中还应当纳入一个更具体或更一般的规定，并且据此来建立这门科学。
——此外，还关乎推理：什么该被纳入、什么该被排除，直到何种界限与范围；而对推理本身来说，最多种多样、最为不同的看法都是敞开的，最终只有任性才能就这些看法下一个确定的规定。
在这种以定义开始一门科学的做法中，并不涉及「应当展示其对象的必然性、从而展示其自身的必然性」这一需要。

en: The concept of pure science and its deduction are therefore presupposed in the present treatise insofar as the Phenomenology of Spirit is nothing other than the deduction of it.

Absolute knowledge is the truth of all the wisdoms of consciousness, because, as that course of it brought it forth, only in absolute knowledge has the separation of the object from the certainty of itself completely resolved itself, and the truth of this certainty as well as this certainty of the truth has become equal.
zh: 因此，在本论述中，纯粹科学的概念及其演绎是被预设的；就此而言，《精神现象学》无非就是它的演绎。
绝对知识是一切意识的智慧的真理，因为正如意识的那条进程所产生的那样，只有在绝对知识中，对象与自我确定性之间的分离才完全解消，而这一确定性的真理以及真理的这一确定性也就变得相等了。

en: Pure science thus presupposes the liberation from the opposition of consciousness.
It contains the thought insofar as it is just as much the thing in itself, or the thing in itself insofar as it is just as much the pure thought.

As science, truth is the pure self-developing self-consciousness and has the shape of the self in that the being-in-and-for-itself is known concept, but the concept as such is the being-in-and-for-itself.
This objective thinking is then the content of pure science.

It is therefore so little formal, it so little lacks the matter for a real and true cognition, that its content is rather solely the absolute true, or, if one would still make use of the word matter, the true matter — but a matter for which form is not something external, since this matter is rather the pure thought and thus the absolute form itself.
Logic is accordingly to be conceived as the system of pure reason, as the realm of pure thought.
This realm is truth as it is in and for itself without a shell.
One can accordingly express it that this content is the representation of God as he is in his eternal essence before the creation of nature and of a finite spirit.
zh: 因此，纯粹科学预设了从意识的对手中解放出来。
它包含思想，就其同样就是事情本身而言；或者说，它包含事情本身，就其同样是纯粹思想而言。
作为科学，真理是纯粹地自我展开的自我意识，它具有自我的形态：自在自为者是知道了的概念，而概念本身则是自在自为者。
所以这种客观思维就是纯粹科学的内容。
因此，它丝毫不是形式的，也丝毫不为现实而真实的认识缺少物质；毋宁说，它的内容恰恰就是绝对的真者，或者，如果人们还想使用「物质」这个词，那就是真正的物质——但这是一种其形式并非外在之物的物质，因为这种物质毋宁就是纯粹思想，因而就是绝对形式本身。
因此，逻辑学应当被把握为纯粹理性的体系、纯粹思想的领域。
这个领域就是真理，是真理脱去外壳而自在自为的样子。
因此人们可以说：这一内容就是上帝的表述——即上帝在创造自然与有限精神之前、其永恒本质中的样子。

en: Anaxagoras is praised as the one who first expressed the thought that the nous, the thought, is the principle of the world, that the essence of the world is to be determined as thought.
He has thereby laid the foundation of an intellectual view of the universe, whose pure shape logic must be.

In it the business is not to think about something which in itself lies outside thinking, about forms which are to be mere marks of truth; rather, the necessary forms and own determinations of thinking are the content and the highest truth itself.
zh: 阿那克萨戈拉被颂为最早说出这一思想的人：nous，即思想，是世界的本原；世界的本质应当被规定为思想。
他由此为一种理智主义的宇宙观奠定了基础，而这种宇宙观的纯粹形态必须是逻辑学。
在逻辑学中，任务并不是去思考某种自在地存在于思维之外的东西、不是去思考那些仅仅充当真理标志的形式；而是：思维的必然形式与思维自己的规定就是内容本身、就是最高的真理。

en: In order at least to take this up into the representation, the opinion is to be set aside that truth must be something tangible.

Such tangibility is, for example, still carried into the Platonic Ideas, which are in the thinking of God, as if they were, so to speak, existent things but in another world or region, outside of which the world of actuality is located and has a real substantiality different from those Ideas and only through this difference.

The Platonic Idea is nothing other than the universal or more precisely the concept of the object; only in its concept does anything have actuality; in so far as it is different from its concept, it ceases to be real and is a nullity; the side of tangibility and sensuous existence-outside-itself belongs to this null side.

— On the other side, however, one can appeal to the very representations of ordinary logic; for it is assumed that definitions, for example, do not contain determinations which fall only into the cognizing subject, but the determinations of the object which constitute its most essential and own nature.

Or if from given determinations one concludes to others, it is assumed that what is concluded is not something external and foreign to the object, but that it belongs to the object itself, that being corresponds to this thinking.

— It lies at the root of the use of the forms of concept, judgement, syllogism, definition, division and so on, that they are not merely forms of self-conscious thinking, but also of the objective understanding.
— Thinking is an expression which attributes the determination contained in it preferentially to consciousness.

But in so far as it is said that understanding, that reason, is in the objective world, that spirit and nature have general laws according to which their life and their changes come about, it is admitted that the determinations of thought have just as much objective worth and existence.
zh: 为了至少把这一点纳入表象，必须先把「真理必须是某种可以上手抓住的东西」这种看法搁在一旁。
例如，这种可以上手抓住的性质甚至被带进了那些处在上帝思维中的柏拉图式观念，仿佛它们乃是（在某种意义上）现成存在的东西，只不过存在于另一个世界或区域；而现实性的世界处在那个区域之外，并且具有一种与那些观念相异的、唯有借着这种相异才成为实在的实体性。
柏拉图式的观念无非是普遍者、更确切地说是对象的概念；只有在它的概念中，某物才有现实性；就它与自己的概念相异而言，它就停止是现实的，并成为一种空无；那种可以上手抓住的方面、那种感性的自在异在的方面，属于这个空无的一面。
——但另一方面，人们可以援引普通逻辑学自身的那些表象；人们确实假定：例如定义并不包含只落入认识主体之中的规定，而是包含对象的那些规定、那些构成对象最本质而最本己的性质的规定。
或者，当人们从给定的规定推论到另一些规定时，人们假定所推论出的东西并不是对对象而言外在而陌生的东西，而是它本身就属于对象，假定存在与这一思维相应。
——概念、判断、推论、定义、划分等诸形式的运用，总体上以这一点为根据：它们不仅是自我意识的思维的形式，而且也是对象性的知性的形式。
——思维是一种表达，它优先地把其中所含的规定归给意识。
但如果说知性、理性存在于对象性的世界中，说精神与自然具有普遍的法则，它们的生命与变化是依照这些法则而发生的，那么也就承认了：思维规定同样具有客观的价值与存在。

en: The critical philosophy did indeed already turn metaphysics into logic, but it, like the later idealism, as was recalled above, out of fear of the object gave the logical determinations an essentially subjective significance; thereby they remained at the same time encumbered with the object which they fled, and a thing-in-itself, an infinite stumbling-block, remained over against them as a beyond.

But the liberation from the opposition of consciousness, which the science must be able to presuppose, elevates the determinations of thought above this anxious, unfinished standpoint and demands the consideration of them as they are in and for themselves, without such a restriction and regard, the logical, the purely rational.
zh: 批判哲学固然已经把形而上学变成了逻辑学，但它和后来的观念论一样，如前所述，出于对客体的惧怕，给逻辑的规定赋予了一种本质上的主观意义；由此，这些规定同时也就仍然沾染着它们所逃避的那个客体，而一个自在之物、一种无穷的阻碍，便作为彼岸留在它们身上。
但是，从意识的这一对立中解放出来——这是科学所必须能够预设的——把思维规定提升到这种怯懦的、未完成的立场之上，并且要求对这些规定作这样的考察：它们自在地、撇开这类限制与顾虑，就是那逻辑的、纯粹理性的东西。
